problem:
Find the radius of convergence $R$ of the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}{x}^{n}}{(3n)!}=1-\frac{x}{3!}+\frac{{x}^{2}}{6!}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{9!}+⋯\,.
$$

feedback.problem:
Find the interval of convergence for the series

$$
{\sum }_{n=0}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{2n+1}}{(n!)^{2}}.
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
To apply the ratio test, we define ${a}_{n}=\frac{{n}^{2}{x}^{n}}{n!}.$ Then, we calculate the ratio of two successive terms and take the limit as $n\to \infty :$

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }|\frac{{x}^{2(n+1)+1}}{((n+1)!)^{2}}\cdot \frac{(n!)^{2}}{{x}^{2n+1}}| \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{(n!)^{2}}{((n+1)!)^{2}}\,{x}^{2} \\  & =|{x}^{2}|{lim}_{n\to \infty }\frac{1}{(n+1)^{2}} \\  & ={x}^{2}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The series converges if $L<1.$ In this case, the convergence condition is satisfied for all $-\infty <x<\infty .$ Therefore, we conclude that the radius of convergence is $R=\infty ,$ and the interval of convergence is $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$
